violations.problem: Rule (red breaker, location identified at panel) matches the scene. Minor and Apprentice are fair.

sources.says: 2022 AHJ checklist: red marking and permanent identification of the breaker at the panel (from existing verification file).

violations.problem: Month/year and a replacement label no more than 4 years after install are both required; scene shows neither. Consistent with entry. Note this label rule is new in the 2022 edition, so an inspector on an older edition would not cite it.

sources.says: Replacement label within four years is a 2022 change (per existing verification file).

violations.problem: Two detectors 38 ft apart is not by itself a violation: the alternative layout rule only needs every point within about 21 ft of a detector, so 38 ft between two neighbours can pass in a narrow room or a staggered layout. An installer would dispute 'spaced too far apart' as stated. The scene needs a layout where it clearly fails. In a square grid at 38 ft, the point at the middle of four detectors is about 27 ft from the nearest one, above 21 ft. Numbers 30, 38, 24 and 21 are consistent with the entry; 24 ft compliant is fine. Severity Major ok; Apprentice is acceptable but borderline (needs the 30 ft figure).

correction.inspectionNote: The open office has a regular grid of ceiling smoke detectors. The floor plan marks neighbouring detectors in the grid 38 feet apart, and the maker's listed spacing for them is 30 feet. The ceiling is smooth and flat, with no beams or ducts, so the spots in the middle of four detectors are about 27 feet from the nearest one, farther than the usual 21 feet.
correction.citations[0].text: On a smooth flat ceiling, spot smoke detectors are normally no more than about 30 feet apart (or the maker's listed spacing if smaller), with a detector within half that distance of each wall. The other way to lay them out is to keep every point on the ceiling within about 21 feet of a detector. Neighbours farther apart than 30 feet in a regular grid fail both tests.
correction.hintText: Pace out the distance between neighbouring detectors in the open office grid and compare it with the usual maximum of about 30 feet, then check how far the middle of four detectors is from the nearest one.

sources.says: Two layout options: listed spacing (30 ft) with half to walls, or all points within 0.7 x spacing (21 ft); 0.7 rule allows wider spacing in some room shapes.
21 ft circle around each detector must cover every point; a 30 ft square sits inside a 42 ft circle.

violations.problem: Shipping caps are not construction protection; sanding dust is exactly the case. Fine. Minor wording risk: if the detectors are capped they are normally not active, so keep 'installed but not active' in mind; the hint says protected, which is fine. Optional tightening of note: 'thin plastic shipping caps'.

correction.inspectionNote: Drywall sanding is under way in the corridor. The installed detectors wear only the thin plastic shipping caps they came with, and a film of dust has settled around them.

sources.says: Shipping covers are for shipping only, not construction protection (from existing verification file).

violations.problem: Owner must receive manual, record drawings and completion record at handover; scene matches. Mild caveat: say it is the final handover so nobody argues drawings follow later.

correction.inspectionNote: The walk-through is ending and the building is being handed over to its owner as finished. The documentation cabinet holds the maker manual and nothing else: no drawings of the installed system and no completion form.

sources.says: 2022 checklist: documentation in 7.5.3.1 delivered to owner.

violations.problem: Dedicated circuit rule clearly broken by a heater on the same circuit. Major is fair. Apprentice would also be defensible since it is obvious, but Journeyman is acceptable.

sources.says: Branch circuit rule 10.6.5.1 for the panel (from existing verification file).

violations.problem: 24 h quiet plus 5 min alarm is the general rule; scene (calc sheet says more amp-hours than installed) breaks it. Caveats: voice systems need 15 min, and some setups with a generator use shorter standby, but scene does not claim these. Minor wording: say the batteries are rated for clearly fewer amp-hours than the sheet requires, which it does.

sources.says: 2022 checklist: 24 hours quiescent and 5 minutes alarm.

violations.problem: Substance right: 75 dBA at the pillow, measured with any intervening door closed; 60 dBA fails. Citation text and hint do not say that the closed door counts, so a learner could argue a corridor horn is fine. Make it explicit. Number consistent (75 vs about 60).

correction.citations[0].text: Where an alarm sounder serves a sleeping area, the sound at the pillow must reach at least 75 dBA, or more where noise around the room is louder. It is measured with any door or curtain between the sounder and the bed in place, so a closed room door counts.
correction.inspectionNote: In the hotel-style sleeping room the only horn and strobe are out in the corridor. With the room door shut and the alarm sounding, the sound meter held at the pillow reads about 60 dBA, well under the 75 dBA minimum.

sources.says: Sleeping area level is the greater of 15 dB over ambient, 5 dB over loudest 60 s noise, or 75 dBA at pillow; if a door or barrier is between the appliance and the pillow, measure with it in place.
AHJ guide on sleeping area sound level requirements.

violations.problem: (1) componentType says 'Initiating Circuit' but the scene is a horn and strobe (notification) circuit; fix. (2) Description claims 'break or ground' but the test only lifts a wire, so say break. (3) Trouble indication is allowed up to 200 seconds, so 'stays quiet' needs a wait or an installer will say you did not wait. (4) Same-room, in-conduit sounder circuits are excused, which the scene avoids by running across the floor. Severity Critical is on the high side (Major would match other unsupervised-system items) but defensible as it hides failures; leave to owner.

correction.description: A horn and strobe circuit is not monitored, so a single break gives no trouble signal
correction.inspectionNote: The installer lifts one wire at the end of a horn and strobe circuit that runs across the office floor, away from the control {term:panel}. After waiting several minutes, the {term:panel} still shows no trouble light and gives no trouble sound.
correction.hintText: Disconnect one wire at the last device on the circuit, wait a few minutes, and watch the control unit.

sources.says: Single open or single ground fault must show as trouble within 200 seconds on monitored wiring.

violations.problem: A new device must be tested after it is added; log empty and never operated is a clear violation. Note the added-device wording was not seen in the 2022 text itself (long-standing rule).

sources.says: 14.4.2 is the reacceptance testing section (from existing verification file).

violations.problem: Owner or representative must be told when part of the system is out of service; scene says owner not informed. The scene also notes a missing log entry (a separate record rule) but the note's main failing is the notice, so it stays on target. Optional: say the zone has been disabled for some time so it is clearly a real impairment rather than a brief test.

correction.inspectionNote: One zone has been showing a disabled light on the control {term:panel} for some time. The impairment log beside it has no entry, and the contractor note on the door says the owner has not been informed.

sources.says: Owner or representative notified when a system or part is impaired; out-of-service events count; record kept 1 year; owner and AHJ told when it ends.

violations.problem: 25 percent (1.25) aging factor is correct for the 2022 edition; earlier edition used 20 percent, so an inspector on an older edition would dispute it. Keep but make sure the profile is the 2022 edition. Master/subtle fits.

sources.says: 2022: safety margin raised from 20 percent to 25 percent (1.25 factor).
Shift from 20 percent margin to 1.25 correction factor in 2022.

violations.problem: Rule is right and the scene sets the authority requirement so it is conditional correctly. Difficulty: this is an obvious scene (letter says fire watch, nobody patrols); Master is too high, Journeyman fits, and isSubtle false agrees. 'Fire watch log' is common practice, not the rule itself; ok as a scene detail.

sources.says: Where the authority requires it, mitigating measures are put in place while impaired, from occupant notice to a full-time fire watch.

violations.problem: Rule fits: out and return together the whole run defeats Class A. Wording nit: 'a single cut would take out both' is fine. The entry says short stretches are allowed, and the scene is the whole run, so it is clearly outside. Hint should not imply a particular distance. Master and subtle fit.

correction.description: The return conductor of a Class A circuit runs in the same raceway as the outgoing one for the whole run
correction.hintText: Follow the Class A circuit out and back through the ceiling space and see whether the two wires ever take separate routes.

sources.says: Outgoing and return conductors routed separately; sharing allowed only up to about 10 ft at devices or panel enclosures (from existing verification file).

overall: 10 of 14 fine on substance; real fixes: detector spacing (38 ft between two neighbours can pass the 21 ft alternative, so set a grid scene), sleeping level (state closed door counts), circuit monitor (notification not initiating, wait up to 200 s, break only), fire watch difficulty Master to Journeyman. Small wording tweaks on construction, records, impairment, Class A. Evidence is trade and AHJ summaries plus prior NFPA draft verification; the standard text itself was not readable.
